title: I Want a Sober Mind
description: I Want a Sober Mind in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 416 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “For a Right Spirit”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: I want a so-ber mind, A self re-nounc-ing will, That tram-ples down and casts be_-hind The baits of pleas-ing ill; A soul in-ured to pain, To hard-ship, grief and loss, Bold to take up, firm to sus-tain The con-se-cra-ted cross.

lines: That tramples down and casts behind
Bold to take up, firm to sustain
That looks to thee when sin is near,
To thee and thy great name;
A pure desire that all may learn

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
